mainTopic: תשלומין of עצרת, the source and limits of the ban on work on חול המועד, and eulogy on the יום טבוח
overview: The amud first explains why the teaching of רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא is needed: without it we would not know that עצרת has seven makeup days (תשלומין). ריש לקיש tries to prove תשלומין from the name ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״, but רבי יוחנן shows from ״חַג הָאָסִיף״ that these names only describe the season of the חג. The גמרא infers that both hold work on חול המועד is forbidden, and asks for the source. Several ברייתות answer. רבי יאשיה learns it from ״תִּשְׁמוֹר״. רבי יונתן uses a קל וחומר and defends it against challenges from the weekdays and ראש חודש. רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא each bring a פסוק. A last ברייתא learns from ״עֲצֶרֶת״ that only some work is forbidden on חול המועד, and that the details are given to the חכמים. Finally, the גמרא resolves a contradiction between the משנה, which allows eulogy on the יום טבוח, and רבי טרפון, who forbade it: the answer depends on which day of the week שבועות fell.

steps.title: Why רבי אלעזר's teaching is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining that the earlier source alone would leave us unsure how many makeup days there are, so רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי אושעיא is needed to teach the number.
steps.simpleTranslation: Without it, I would not know how many days there are. So it teaches us this through the statement that רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous discussion. It explains why we need רבי אלעזר's teaching about the makeup days of עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From another source alone we might know that עצרת has תשלומין, but not how many days. רבי אלעזר's teaching fills that gap and tells us there are seven.

phrases.english: I would not know how many
phrases.notes: He means how many makeup days the קרבנות of עצרת can still be brought.

phrases.english: it teaches us
through what Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא יָדַעְנָא כַּמָּה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier explanation of why each source for תשלומין is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר's teaching is needed to fix the number of makeup days at seven.

steps.title: ריש לקיש reads the name ״חג הקציר״
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש offers a different source: ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ means a חג on which you both celebrate and harvest, and that is עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: ״And the festival of harvest.″ Which festival do you celebrate and also harvest on? You must say this is עצרת.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש starts a new proof for the makeup days of עצרת. He reads the name ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ to mean a חג that has harvesting on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He takes the name literally: a holiday that involves both celebrating and harvesting. He identifies that holiday as עצרת and sets up the question of which day he means.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
“And the festival of harvest”
Which festival is it
that you celebrate and also harvest on?
You must say this is Atzeret.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for תשלומין of עצרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ describes עצרת as a חג on which there is harvesting.

steps.title: Harvesting must mean the makeup days
steps.stepSummary: Harvesting is forbidden on יום טוב, so ריש לקיש concludes the פסוק must refer to the makeup days of עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this? If you say on יום טוב itself, is harvesting allowed on יום טוב? Rather, isn't it talking about the makeup days?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש asks which day the harvesting could happen on. He proves it must be the makeup days, since harvesting on יום טוב is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day of עצרת itself is יום טוב, and harvesting is not allowed then. So the only days of this חג when harvesting is allowed are the תשלומין days, and the פסוק hints that they exist.

keyTerms.meaning: makeup days for bringing the חג's קרבנות

phrases.english: When?
If you say on the Yom Tov itself
is harvesting on Yom Tov permitted?
Rather, isn't it talking about the makeup days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's proof by ruling out the day of יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The name ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ together with the ban on harvesting on יום טוב

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's parallel: ״חג האסיף״
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן applies the same reasoning to ״חַג הָאָסִיף״ (סוכות) and shows it fails, since gathering is not allowed on יום טוב or on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: But if so, ״the festival of gathering″: which festival has gathering? You must say it is סוכות. When? If you say on יום טוב, is work allowed on יום טוב? Rather, on חול המועד. But is work allowed on חול המועד?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש by running the same reasoning on a parallel name. With סוכות, that reasoning leads to a dead end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ means harvesting happens on the חג, then ״חַג הָאָסִיף״ should mean gathering happens on סוכות. But gathering is forbidden on יום טוב and also on חול המועד, so the literal reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (introduces a challenge from a parallel)
the intermediate days of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying work is allowed on חול המועד. His question ״is it permitted?״ means it is not, and that is exactly why the parallel fails.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
But if so, “the festival of gathering”:

phrases.aramaic: אֵי זֶהוּ חַג שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אֲסִיפָה —
phrases.english: which festival has gathering on it?
You must say this is the festival of Sukkot.
When? If you say on Yom Tov
is work on Yom Tov permitted?
Rather, on the intermediate days.
Is work on the intermediate days permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's reading by applying it to a parallel phrase.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's literal reading of ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading of ״חַג הָאָסִיף״ would need gathering on סוכות, but no day of סוכות allows such work.

steps.title: The names describe the season
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן concludes that ״חַג הָאָסִיף״ means the חג that falls in the gathering season, so ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ means the חג that falls in harvest season, and there is no proof for תשלומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a festival that comes at the time of gathering. Here too, it means a festival that comes at the time of harvest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the right way to read these names. Doing so removes ריש לקיש's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The names tell us when in the year the חג comes, not that work is done on it. So ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ does not point to makeup days, and ריש לקיש's source is pushed aside.
steps.whatToRemember: ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״ and ״חַג הָאָסִיף״ are names of seasons, so ריש לקיש's proof for תשלומין does not hold.

phrases.english: Rather, it means a festival that comes at the time of gathering;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי — חַג הַבָּא בִּזְמַן קְצִירָה.
phrases.english: here too, a festival that comes at the time of harvest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יוחנן's challenge with the correct reading.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's proof for תשלומין from ״חַג הַקָּצִיר״
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The name describes the season of the חג, not days when harvesting is allowed.

steps.title: Both hold work on חול המועד is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from this exchange that both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש hold that work on חול המועד is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: This shows that both of them hold that doing work on חול המועד is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a side lesson from the argument it just saw. Both אמוראים agree that work on חול המועד is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's challenge works only if work on חול המועד is forbidden. ריש לקיש did not argue with that point, so he must agree too.

keyTerms.meaning: it follows that / we can infer

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a source for the view that the ban on work on חול המועד is serious enough to be assumed by both אמוראים.

phrases.english: This shows that both of them hold
that the intermediate festival days are forbidden
for doing work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side inference from the shared assumption of the exchange.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש hold that work on חול המועד is forbidden.

steps.title: Where does the ban on work during the middle days come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that work is forbidden on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just concluded that work on חול המועד is forbidden. Now it asks where that rule comes from, which sets up the ברייתות that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that two אמוראים agree on a rule is not enough. The גמרא wants a source from the תורה or from logic. Everything after this line answers this question.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things known? (asking for a source)
The middle days of a יום טוב

phrases.english: From where are these things known?
phrases.notes: "These things" means the rule from the last step: work on חול המועד is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the conclusion reached in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that work is forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה learns it from the word 'guard'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי יאשיה learns the איסור from ״את חג המצות תשמור שבעת ימים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "You shall guard the חג המצות for seven days." This teaches that work is forbidden on חול המועד. These are the words of רבי יאשיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. רבי יאשיה says that the command to guard the חג for all seven days includes the middle days, so work on them is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק covers all seven days, not only the first and last. Guarding the whole חג for seven days includes not working on the middle days.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"You shall guard the festival of matzos seven days"
this teaches about חול המועד
that doing work is forbidden,
these are the words of רבי יאשיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 with a first source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word תשמור, applied to all seven days, forbids work on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי יונתן proves it with logic instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says no פסוק is needed. A קל וחומר shows that the middle days, which have holy days on both sides, should be at least as strict as the first and seventh days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יונתן says: it is not needed, because a קל וחומר teaches it. The first and seventh days have no holiness before or after them, yet work on them is forbidden. So the middle days, which have holiness before and after them, should surely have work forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן offers a different source. He argues from logic, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day before the first day and the day after the seventh day are ordinary weekdays. The middle days are surrounded by holy days on both sides. If the less-surrounded days forbid work, the more-surrounded days should too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (we don't need this source)
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
Holiness before them and after them

phrases.english: רבי יונתן says: it is not needed,
it comes from a קל וחומר:
if the first and seventh days,
which have no holiness before and after them,
have doing work forbidden,
then חול המועד,
which has holiness before and after it,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיְּהֵא אָסוּר בַּעֲשִׂיַּית מְלָאכָה.
phrases.english: isn't it logical that doing work should be forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a logical source in place of רבי יאשיה's פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קל וחומר from the first and seventh days proves that work is forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.title: Challenge: the six weekdays also sit between holy days
steps.stepSummary: The six days of the week are surrounded by שבת on both sides, yet work on them is permitted. So 'holiness on both sides' cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The six weekdays will prove otherwise: they have holiness before and after them, and work on them is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יונתן's קל וחומר with a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר depends on the idea that being surrounded by holy days makes a day stricter. Ordinary weekdays sit between two שבתות, yet work on them is allowed. That breaks the logic.

keyTerms.meaning: The six days of Creation, meaning the ordinary weekdays

phrases.english: The six weekdays will prove it,
since they have holiness before and after them,
phrases.notes: The holiness here is שבת, which comes right before and right after the weekdays.

phrases.english: and yet doing work on them is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר of step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Weekdays are surrounded by holiness, yet work on them is allowed. So surrounding holiness does not create an איסור.

steps.title: Answer: the middle days have a קרבן מוסף
steps.stepSummary: Weekdays have no קרבן מוסף, but חול המועד does. So חול המועד carries its own holiness that weekdays lack.
steps.simpleTranslation: Weekdays have no extra offering. Can you say the same about חול המועד, which does have an extra offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the קל וחומר by showing that weekdays are different from חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן מוסף shows that חול המועד has some holiness of its own. Weekdays have nothing like that, so they cannot serve as a counterexample.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (pointing out how the compared case is different)
The extra offering brought on special days

phrases.english: What about the six weekdays?
They have no extra offering.
Would you say the same about חול המועד,
which has an extra offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Weekdays show that surrounding holiness means nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: חול המועד has a קרבן מוסף, which gives it a holiness that weekdays lack.

steps.title: Challenge: ראש חודש has a קרבן מוסף, yet work is allowed
steps.stepSummary: ראש חודש has a קרבן מוסף, but work on it is permitted. So the מוסף alone cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראש חודש will prove otherwise: it has an extra offering, and work on it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with a new counterexample against the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a קרבן מוסף were enough to forbid work, ראש חודש would also forbid work. It doesn't, so the distinction from step 11 seems too weak.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of a new month

phrases.english: ראש חודש will prove it,
since it has an extra offering,
and yet doing work on it is permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a קרבן מוסף makes חול המועד strict
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ראש חודש has a מוסף, yet work on it is allowed.

steps.title: Answer: the middle days are called 'מקרא קודש'
steps.stepSummary: ראש חודש is not called מקרא קודש, but חול המועד is. Because of that name, it makes sense that work is forbidden. The קל וחומר stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: ראש חודש is not called a 'holy gathering.' Can you say the same about חול המועד, which is called a 'holy gathering'? Since it is called a 'holy gathering,' it is logical that work is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ראש חודש challenge and closes רבי יונתן's argument successfully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה gives חול המועד the title מקרא קודש but never gives it to ראש חודש. That title separates חול המועד from both counterexamples, so work on it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy gathering, a title the תורה gives to the festival days

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יונתן's קל וחומר survives two challenges. Weekdays have no מוסף, and ראש חודש is not called מקרא קודש. חול המועד has both, so work on it is forbidden.

phrases.english: What about ראש חודש?
It is not called "a holy gathering."
Would you say the same about חול המועד,
which is called "a holy gathering"?
Since it is called "a holy gathering,"
it is logical that doing work is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 and completes the defense of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ראש חודש shows that a מוסף alone means nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: חול המועד is called מקרא קודש, which ראש חודש is not. So work on it is forbidden.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי's פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns the איסור from ״כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: "You shall do no laborious work." This teaches that work is forbidden on חול המועד. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that gives a different פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new source, separate from the first ברייתא. רבי יוסי הגלילי reads this פסוק as covering the middle days.

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches:
"You shall do no laborious work"
this teaches about חול המועד
that doing work is forbidden,
these are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the question of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״כל מלאכת עבודה לא תעשו״ forbids work on חול המועד.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא points to a different פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says that פסוק is not needed, because ״אלה מועדי ה׳״ teaches the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: it is not needed. The תורה already says: "These are the appointed festivals of ה׳..."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא offers his own source. This line sets up his proof, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far רבי עקיבא only names the פסוק. He explains how it proves the rule in the next step.

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא says: it is not needed,
for the פסוק already says:
"These are the appointed festivals of ה׳, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:4. The "etc." points to the rest of the פסוק, which calls these days מקרא קודש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי's source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״אלה מועדי ה׳״ is the source for the איסור on חול המועד.

steps.title: Proof by elimination: it must mean the middle days
steps.stepSummary: The first and seventh days are already called שבתון elsewhere, so this פסוק must be about חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the פסוק talking about? If the first day, it already said 'a day of rest.' If the seventh day, it already said 'a day of rest.' So the פסוק must be talking about חול המועד, to teach you that work is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא explains his proof. He rules out the first and seventh days one by one, so only the middle days are left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat itself for no reason. The first and seventh days already have their own word, שבתון. A פסוק that does not come to teach about them must be teaching about the middle days.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק talking about?

phrases.english: What is the פסוק talking about?
If the first day, it has already said "a day of rest" about it,
if the seventh day, it has already said "a day of rest" about it.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: So the פסוק must be talking only about חול המועד,
to teach you that doing work is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the פסוק cited in step 15 proves the rule.
steps.raayaObject: Work is forbidden on חול המועד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ״אלה מועדי ה׳״, read by elimination, since the first and seventh days are already called שבתון.

steps.title: A third ברייתא: the six days are like the seventh
steps.stepSummary: From ״ששת ימים תאכל מצות וביום השביעי עצרת לה׳״, the ברייתא learns that just as the seventh day is held back from work, so are the six days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: "Six days you shall eat מצות, and on the seventh day there shall be a holy assembly to ה׳." Just as the seventh day is held back from work, so too the six days are held back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא with yet another source, comparing the six days of פסח to the seventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the six days and the seventh day together. So the ברייתא applies the seventh day's holding back from work to the six days as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A holy assembly; from the root meaning 'to hold back'

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches:
"Six days you shall eat matzos,
and on the seventh day a holy assembly to ה׳."
Just as the seventh day is held back,
so too the six days are held back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the question of step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The six days are compared to the seventh, so work is forbidden on them.

steps.title: Challenge: then all work would be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If the six days are just like the seventh, they should be held back from every kind of work, just like the seventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so: just as the seventh day is held back from all work, the six days should also be held back from all work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison it just made. If the comparison is complete, then all work would be forbidden on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seventh day forbids every kind of work. A full comparison would make חול המועד exactly as strict. The next step answers this from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as the גמרא's final ruling that all work is forbidden on חול המועד. It is a challenge to the comparison.

phrases.aramaic: אִי: מָה שְׁבִיעִי עָצוּר בְּכׇל מְלָאכָה —
phrases.english: If so: just as the seventh day is held back from all work,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עֲצוּרִין בְּכׇל מְלָאכָה.
phrases.english: so too the six days should be held back from all work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה שְׁבִיעִי עָצוּר בְּכׇל מְלָאכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of the six days to the seventh made in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the six days and the seventh day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would forbid every kind of work on חול המועד, just as on the seventh day.

steps.title: Only the seventh day is closed to all work
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers the challenge from Step 18. The word עצרת is said only about the seventh day, so only that day is closed to every kind of work. The six days of חול המועד are closed to only some work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And on the seventh day there shall be a holding back." The seventh day is held back from all work, but the six days are not held back from all work.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from Step 18: if חול המועד is like the seventh day, why isn't all work forbidden on it? The answer is that the verse gives full 'holding back' to the seventh day alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison in Step 17 still holds: חול המועד is 'held back' from work. But the verse singles out the seventh day as עצרת, so the full ban belongs only to that day. On the six days only part of the work is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A holding back, a day closed off from work

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And on the seventh day there shall be a holding back,"
the seventh day is held back from all work,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין שִׁשָּׁה יָמִים עֲצוּרִין בְּכׇל מְלָאכָה.
phrases.english: but the six days are not held back from all work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a verse by its exact wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since חול המועד is compared to the seventh day, all work should be forbidden on it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the seventh day is called עצרת for all work. The six days are restricted from only some work.

steps.title: The תורה leaves the details to the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: Because the תורה does not say which work is forbidden on חול המועד, the details are given over to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the verse handed the matter over only to the חכמים, to tell you which day is forbidden and which is permitted, which work is forbidden and which work is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up its point. Since only some work is forbidden on חול המועד and the תורה does not list which, the חכמים decide the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on work in חול המועד has a source in the תורה, but its exact limits are left to the חכמים. They decide which work is forbidden and which is allowed. They also decide which days the rules apply to.
steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד some work is forbidden, but not all of it. The תורה gives the job of deciding which work to the חכמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for why the detailed rules of work on חול המועד come from the חכמים, even though the ban itself is rooted in the תורה.

phrases.english: So the verse handed them over
only to the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לָךְ אֵי זֶה יוֹם אָסוּר
phrases.english: to tell you which day is forbidden
and which day is permitted,
which work is forbidden
and which work is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הא לא מסרן הכתוב אלא לחכמים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the answer in Step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The details of forbidden work on חול המועד are given over to the חכמים.

steps.title: Eulogy and fasting allowed on the day of slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back the משנה's rule: when the יום טבוח after שבועות falls on Sunday, eulogy and fasting are allowed. This is so that people will not seem to support those who said שבועות always falls after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they are permitted to eulogize and fast, so as not to support the words of those who say that עצרת falls after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the משנה. This sets up a question that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day after שבועות is a day when the holiday offerings could still be brought. If שבועות fell on שבת, that day would be Sunday. Treating it like a holiday would look like agreeing with the group who said שבועות always falls on Sunday, so the משנה allows eulogy and fasting.

keyTerms.meaning: Eulogy, mourning speech for someone who died
The false claim that שבועות always falls on the day after שבת

phrases.english: And they are permitted to eulogize and to fast,
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה, which is talking about the day of slaughter after שבועות.

phrases.english: so as not to support the words of those who say
that Atzeres is after Shabbos.
phrases.notes: עצרת here means שבועות. These people claimed it must always fall on Sunday.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eulogy and fasting are allowed on the יום טבוח after שבועות, to push back against the group who said שבועות always falls on Sunday.

steps.title: רבי טרפון stopped a eulogy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story that seems to contradict the משנה. When אלכסא died in לוד, רבי טרפון did not allow a eulogy because of the day of עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught: Once אלכסא died in לוד, and all Israel came to eulogize him, but רבי טרפון did not let them, because it was the יום טוב of עצרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a story. In the story, a eulogy was stopped because of עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says eulogy is allowed on the day after שבועות. But רבי טרפון stopped a eulogy because of עצרת. This seems to be a contradiction. The next two steps check the story's exact wording, and step 25 resolves it.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it stated, used to bring a source that seems to contradict
An incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated:
There was an incident: Alexa died in Lod,
and all Israel gathered to eulogize him,
but Rabbi Tarfon did not let them,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיּוֹם טוֹב שֶׁל עֲצֶרֶת הָיָה.
phrases.english: because it was the Yom Tov of Atzeres.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that eulogy and fasting are allowed on the יום טבוח after שבועות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון stopped a eulogy because of עצרת, which seems to go against the משנה's permission.

steps.title: It could not have been the holiday itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording of the story. People would never gather for a eulogy on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think it was יום טוב? If it was יום טוב, would they have come?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question the story's wording. It points out that the story cannot be talking about the actual holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a eulogy is not held on יום טוב, so the whole community would not have gathered for one. That means the word 'יום טוב' in the story cannot mean the holiday itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (a way of saying: that can't be right)

phrases.english: Would it enter your mind that it was Yom Tov?
If it was on Yom Tov, would they have come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the story brought in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'יום טוב של עצרת' in the story
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No one would gather for a eulogy on the holiday itself, so the story cannot mean the actual holiday.

steps.title: Read it as the day of slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the story's wording. It was the יום טבוח, the day after שבועות, and that makes the contradiction with the משנה even stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: because it was the day of slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the story so that it makes sense. The fixed version now clashes directly with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the story is read as the יום טבוח, it is talking about the same day as the משנה. The משנה allows eulogy on that day, but רבי טרפון forbade it. So the contradiction is now clear and needs an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of slaughter, the day after שבועות when holiday offerings could still be brought

steps.confusionAlert: Fixing the wording does not solve the problem. It makes the contradiction with the משנה sharper, and the real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
because it was the day of slaughter!
phrases.notes: This is the day after שבועות, when people could still bring their holiday offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אימא: מפני שיום טבוח היה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 by correcting the wording, which brings back the challenge from Step 22 in a sharper form.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story says it was the holiday itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The story was about the יום טבוח, which clashes directly with the משנה.

steps.title: It depends on which day שבועות fell
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. רבי טרפון's story is about a year when שבועות fell after שבת. The משנה is about a year when שבועות fell on שבת, which puts the day of slaughter on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it is about a יום טוב that falls after שבת. There, it is about a יום טוב that falls on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The משנה and the story are talking about different years in the calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When שבועות falls on שבת, the day of slaughter is Sunday. Treating it as a holiday would look like agreeing with the group who said שבועות is always on Sunday, so eulogy is allowed. In other years there is no such worry, so the day of slaughter keeps some of the holiday's honor, and רבי טרפון did not allow a eulogy.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no contradiction
Here... there (each source is about a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: Eulogy on the יום טבוח is allowed when it falls on Sunday, as when שבועות falls on שבת. When שבועות falls after שבת, the יום טבוח keeps some holiday honor, and eulogy is not allowed.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it is about a Yom Tov
phrases.notes: This 'here' is רבי טרפון's story in לוד.

phrases.english: that falls after Shabbos,
there, it is about a Yom Tov
phrases.notes: This 'there' is the משנה, where the day of slaughter lands on Sunday.

phrases.english: that falls on Shabbos.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא קשיא: כאן ביום טוב שחל להיות אחר השבת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the משנה and the corrected story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (each source is about a different situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רבי טרפון disagree about eulogy on the יום טבוח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about years when the day of slaughter falls on Sunday. רבי טרפון's story is about other years.
